hook.line: The apology that lands after a hard conversation names what you did. Spanish does it in one short chain: *siento*, then *haber*, then the thing.
hook.en: I'm sorry I didn't listen to you.

examples.en: I'm sorry I didn't let you know sooner. (to a friend)
I'm very sorry I was late.
I'm sorry I shouted at you. (to a friend)
I regret not having come yesterday.

examples.es: Siento no haber dicho la verdad.
examples.en: I'm sorry I didn't tell the truth.

rule:
To apologise for something you did, use *siento* or *lamento*, then *haber* and the *-ado* or *-ido* form of the verb: *Siento haberte gritado*.

For something you didn't do, put *no* first: *Siento no haberte avisado*.

English says "I'm sorry I shouted" with two clauses. Spanish keeps one doer, so there is no *que* and no second conjugated verb. Pronouns stick to the end of *haber*: *haberte*. *Lamento* sounds a little more formal.
smallPrint: Teachers call *haber* plus the *-ado* form the perfect infinitive. It looks back at something already done.

options: I'm sorry you shouted at me.
I'm sorry to shout at you.
I'm sorry I shouted at you.
I'm sorry I didn't let you know sooner.
I'm sorry you didn't let me know.
I'm sorry I let you know too soon.
I'm afraid I'll lose control.
I regret that you lost control.
I regret losing control.
I'm very sorry you were late.
I'm very sorry I was late.
I'm very sorry I'm early.
I regret coming yesterday.
I regret that you didn't come yesterday.
I regret not having come yesterday.

readAndPick.es: Siento no haber dicho la verdad.
options: I'm sorry I told the truth.
I'm sorry I didn't tell the truth.
I'm sorry you didn't tell the truth.

readAndPick.es: Siento mucho no haber estado contigo.
options: I'm so sorry I wasn't with you.
I'm so sorry I was with you.
I'm so sorry you weren't with me.
I'm sorry you bothered me.
I'm sorry I didn't bother you.
I'm sorry I bothered you.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right form and type the whole sentence: *Siento ___ tarde.* (*haber llegado* or *llegué*)
yourTurn.why: The thing you did follows *siento* as *haber* plus the *-ado* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I'm sorry I didn't let you know sooner.
yourTurn.why: *No* goes first, and *te* sticks to the end of *haber*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I'm sorry I shouted at you.
yourTurn.why: One doer, so *haber gritado*, with *te* attached.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I regret not having come yesterday.
Make it negative: *Siento haber dicho la verdad.* Say: I'm sorry I didn't tell the truth.
yourTurn.answer: Siento no haber dicho la verdad.
accept: Lamento no haber dicho la verdad.
yourTurn.why: Put *no* in front of *haber*, not in front of *siento*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a little more formal: *Siento haberte molestado.* Swap the first verb.
yourTurn.why: *Lamento* is the slightly more formal choice.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I'm very sorry I wasn't with you.
yourTurn.answer: Siento mucho no haber estado contigo.
accept: Lamento mucho no haber estado contigo.

pitfalls.wrong: Siento que no te avisé antes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. When you are the one who did it, Spanish uses *haber* and the *-ado* form, not a second clause.
Almost. The pronoun attaches to the end of *haber*.
Almost. After *haber* comes the *-ado* form, not the infinitive.

personal: Say one thing you're sorry you did, or didn't do, this week. Start with *Siento…* or *Lamento…*
